version.changelog: Rewrite concurrent write protection section: broaden from Feishu-only to universal pattern (Excel/local files/APIs all share the same root cause). Add problem panorama table, unified protection rules, and three iron laws: single writer, incremental over full, parallel read serial write.

llm.summary: The skill is mostly coherent as a complex-task orchestration helper, but it requires broad persistent logging of user task details and ships a checkpoint script with an unvalidated file path risk.

dimensions.detail: File writes, sub-agent spawning, external document writes, and script execution are plausible for orchestration, but the guidance is broad and the checkpoint helper accepts task IDs directly in filesystem paths.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, dependency fetch, remote payload retrieval, tool replacement, service registration, or automatic execution mechanism was found in the inspected artifacts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill mandates writing the user's requirements, source, plan, key parameters, document tokens, file paths, and status to daily notes or work logs before any action, without a clear consent gate, redaction rule, or path/retention boundary.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent daily notes and checkpoint files are central to the design. This is disclosed and purpose-aligned for recovery, but the required content can include sensitive task details and the checkpoint script can read or write JSON files outside its intended directory via path traversal.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core purpose, complex task decomposition with checkpointing, file outputs, progress recovery, and limited sub-agent use, matches the documented capability. External Feishu writes, Python script execution, and configuration/deployment examples are purpose-adjacent but need user-directed use.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing if your tasks may include secrets, customer data, document tokens, business plans, or sensitive file paths. Use it only with clear workspace boundaries, avoid recording raw sensitive details in daily notes, and do not run the checkpoint helper with untrusted task IDs until its path validation is fixed.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: File reads and writes are expected for checkpointing and WAL-style orchestration, but the artifact does not define tight allowed paths or tool boundaries.
[SQP-2] expected: Pre-action logging is explicitly part of the recovery design, but the required fields are broad and include potentially sensitive details without consent, minimization, or retention limits.
[SSD-3] expected: Persistent checkpoints and logs support crash recovery, but the mandatory daily-note logging creates a durable store of user-derived task content.
[SDI-2] expected: Feishu document and wiki creation are only shown in task patterns where document migration or output generation is requested, so they are purpose-aligned, but they are external side-effecting actions that should be explicitly user-directed.
[SQP-1] expected: Some trigger examples are broad, but the main skill description and decision gate narrow activation to complex, multi-step, batch, or long-running tasks; this is a scoping note rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
[SDI-2] expected: Python script writing and execution is recommended for large data processing. That is coherent for batch orchestration, but it should be used only on user-approved inputs in the normal execution sandbox.
[SQP-3] unexpected: The artifacts are Chinese-only. This is a localization and accessibility limitation, not a security basis for escalation by itself.
[T05] unexpected: The checkpoint helper builds paths from an unvalidated task_id, so create, read, and update can escape ~/.openclaw/workspace/checkpoints for JSON-suffixed paths. This is a real implementation risk, though not evidence of intent to exfiltrate or damage data.
